expectedRealization.rationale: The partial tax rollback changes 2017 passenger-vehicle demand comparisons immediately, but cutoff-valid company evidence does not identify a positive event-driven earnings exception.

changeHypothesis.summary: The <=1.6L passenger-vehicle purchase tax rises from 5% to 7.5% in 2017, creating a softer landing than a full return to 10% but a clear demand headwind versus the 2016 stimulus baseline.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: The 7.5% rate is fixed for 2017, so the changed demand baseline persists for a full year.
disconfirmingEvidence: SAIC, Changan and Great Wall all had profitable 2016 operating baselines, but none of the frozen evidence shows a new positive company driver caused by the tax reset.
Changan and Great Wall were benefiting from the prior stimulus cycle.
The auto price regime is only neutral, not a broad fresh positive reset.

evidenceLedger.supportsClaim: The 2017 purchase-tax rate reset creates a new demand baseline.
SAIC entered the event profitable but with declining OCF and no new tax-reset benefit.
Changan's strong 2016 growth was part of the old stimulus-supported baseline.
Great Wall's strong 2016 sales/profit also benefited from the existing demand regime.
The frozen auto basket was neutral at cutoff.

causalChain.mechanism: The consumer tax incentive becomes less generous, creating a tougher 2017 comparison.
causalChain.failureMode: underlying income/product-cycle strength fully offsets the tax change

causalChain.mechanism: Unit volume, pricing and inventory determine whether the tax reset changes revenue/profit.
causalChain.failureMode: company product launches/share gains offset aggregate demand pressure

losers: small-engine OEMs most dependent on stimulus-sensitive demand
substitutes: larger-engine or alternative-powertrain vehicles depending consumer mix
falseThemeMatches: profitable auto OEMs assumed to benefit merely because tax policy is clarified

selectionComparison.rationale: No cutoff-valid company has a positive event-driven earnings bridge strong enough to justify selection after the tax incentive becomes less generous.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: The frozen auto basket was roughly +2.32pp excess over 20d and -0.54pp over 60d, a neutral regime. Company profit strength was already visible before the tax reset.
expectations.thesisExpectation: 2017 demand may soften relative to the 2016 stimulus baseline, with company outcomes driven more by product/share than by the policy event itself.
expectations.measurableGap: No positive company-specific incremental gap is verified.

hypothesisDecompositionTest.productMarketScope: <=1.6L passenger-vehicle demand under the 2017 purchase-tax reset
hypothesisDecompositionTest.rationale: The event is a demand-baseline reset; no company-specific positive exception is sufficiently evidenced in the frozen pool.

nearTerm.driver: partial incentive rollback versus product/company strength

mediumTerm.driver: 2017 tax rate is less supportive than 2016

structural.driver: product/share can offset policy but is company-specific and not a new event bridge

evidenceHorizonMatrix.resolutionRule: No selection until a company-specific product/share driver is separately verified; do not reinterpret policy clarity as positive alpha.

leaderDivergenceTest.rationale: Company quality differs, but no frozen positive event-specific earnings path is established.

bearCase: 2016 stimulus-supported volume was pulled forward and the less generous 2017 tax rate weakens unit growth.

invalidationConditions.threshold: new verified growth engine offsets policy headwind

caveats: No post-cutoff selected-stock outcome is used before lock.

nextResearchActions: No selection; wait for a separate company-specific positive driver rather than treating policy clarification as opportunity.

freshIncrementalDriver.rationale: The event is fresh but is a partial demand headwind, not a positive driver.

realizedEarningsSupport.rationale: OEM earnings are positive but predate the event.

revisionVelocity.rationale: No positive event-specific revision is frozen.

durationMechanism.rationale: The tax rate is fixed for 2017.

highAbsorptionContinuationTest.falsifier: A new company-specific product/share driver emerges.

expressionPurityTest.earningsQualityComparison: Profitable OEMs exist, but quality alone is not an event-specific positive bridge.

adversarialEvidenceTest.strongestCounterThesis: The policy reset is a demand headwind and existing company quality reflects the old stimulus baseline rather than a new opportunity.
adversarialEvidenceTest.falsifierOrEscalationTrigger: A company demonstrates a new product/share/earnings reset that clearly offsets the tax headwind.
